Alex: Quick sync — we need to pick a prioritization and rollout approach for the new dynamic-routing fallback (customer SLA risk). RICE vs impact/effort leanings? Also proposing a 3-stage experiment: small canary -> progressive ramp -> A/B feature flag for 10%/50%/100%. Thoughts?
Priya: RICE makes sense but we should separate risk (S). I'm proposing Reach=5, Impact=8, Confidence=6, Effort=13. RICE = (5*8*6)/13 ≈ 18.5. Confidence is low because we haven't stress-tested kv-cache interactions. :thinking:
Marco: I lean impact/effort matrix for quick tradeoffs — easier to visualize sprint trade. RICE useful for intake scoring but noisy for sequencing. For rollout: prefer 2 canaries (internal alpha -> external 1%) then A/B.
Sam: Ops note: must add circuit-breaker + automatic fallback to previous policy. Also need per-customer concurrency caps to avoid noisy-neighbor blowups. + on-call paging rules. :warning:
Lina: Engineering constraint: we can ship the minimal fallback (MVP) in 2 sprints, full observability + throttles in 5. So scope should be split MVP vs Full.
Alex: OK, here's a concrete proposed plan:
```
Phase 0: internal canary (100% internal traffic for 24h)
Phase 1: public canary (1% traffic, 48h)
Phase 2: ramp (10% -> 50% over 3 days)
Phase 3: A/B test (50/50 for 2 weeks) + quality evaluation
Guardrails: automatic rollback to previous policy if error rate > 0.5% OR latency p95 increases by >30%
Observability: token-level traces + per-route SLO dashboards
```
Priya: Add explicit launch criteria: metrics stable for 48h, zero regressions on critical prompt set, SLOs met, engineering sign-off, and runbook completed. Also tie quality checks to our eval harness.
Marco: On prioritization, propose hybrid approach: use RICE for intake prioritization, then impact/effort matrix during sprint planning to negotiate scope. Also, for customer-driven asks, weight Reach higher if >3 enterprise customers requested.
Sam: Ops runbook needs: rollback command, who to page, and a quick mitigation checklist. Example snippet: `./scripts/rollback.sh --env prod --tag v2` and run `./monitor/check-slo.sh --route /dynamic-route`.
Lina: Can we include a soft cost quota so if inference cost spikes we auto-cap throughput? Implementation idea: token-based throttle per customer + default global rate cap.
Alex: Decision checklist for this thread:
- Prioritization method: hybrid (RICE intake, impact/effort for sequencing)
- Rollout: phased canary + progressive ramp + A/B with automatic rollback
- Safety: circuit-breaker, token throttles, cost guardrails, runbook, pager list
- Owners: @Lina (rollout infra), @Priya (metrics & launch criteria), @Sam (ops/runbook)
- Timeline: start internal canary next Tue (tentative)
Priya: I'll document the MVP vs Full scope and add launch criteria to the roadmap doc. We should also list which enterprise customers get early opt-in.
Marco: I'll update the prioritization spreadsheet with conservative confidence and split effort into MVP/Full. Scheduling a 30m alignment next Monday to finalize thresholds. :calendar:
deploy-bot: Deployment ticket created: #deploy-4532 — scheduled window Tue 09:00 UTC.
Alex: Perfect — thanks everyone. I'll put the checklist into the roadmap doc and tag stakeholders. :rocket:
